spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Mere
spec.description: A colossal five-headed Norse-style hydra in a God of War look: scarred slate-green hide, bone horns, iron-bound leather and broken weapons embedded in its flesh, with ember, frost and venom runes glowing on each head.
spec.layout: A huge four-legged beast, centred on x=0 and facing +Z. A heavy barrel torso (z -2.4..2.3, top about y 3.4) stands on four thick reptilian legs; rear legs are digitigrade and bigger, front legs are shoulder-heavy with big clawed paws. A long thick tail trails behind to z -6.8 and the tip rests on the floor. FIVE long muscular necks rise from the shoulder hump (z about 1.3..1.7) and fan out like a hand, each ending in a head that looks forward and slightly down. The centre head (C) is the tallest and biggest: skull top y about 5.9, horns to y 6.4, snout to z 4.6. The inner heads (IL at +x, IR at -x) sit about x ±1.75, y 5.1, and are a little smaller. The outer heads (OL at +x, OR at -x) hang lower and wider at x ±2.85, y 4.3, with necks curving outward then forward. From the front the five necks read as a spread fan with a clear gap between each pair. Hide: dark slate-green scales (scaleDark back, scaleMid flanks, scaleLight highlights on ridges) over a bone-yellow belly and throat made of broad plates. God of War style: brutal, heavy and angular; chunky blocky plates, a desaturated cold palette with small hot accents; deep scars with pale ridged edges; Norse rune glyphs carved as small straight-stroke parts; broken axe heads, spear shafts, arrowheads, iron-bound leather straps and chain remnants embedded in the body. Ember orange (fire), frost blue and venom green glow only on small parts: eyes, nostrils, runes and cracks. Each head has its own identity: C = ember crown, IL = frost, IR = venom, OL = ember, OR = bone and iron muzzle. Mouths are rest-pose slightly open: the lower jaw hangs about 8 degrees below the upper. Every surface is one flat colour; scars, runes, teeth, eyes, straps and rivets are small parts seated on the surface. Use the glow kit on ember, frost, venom and eye parts.

parts.builds: The torso and the front half. (1) Torso: one loft through the mount torsoStations_zYWH (each entry is z, centre y, full width, full height), flat-box-ish and heavy, skinned to [hips, chest]. Painted by sector: scaleDark back, scaleMid flanks, belly/bellyDark underside as broad separate bone-yellow ventral plates (a row of 8 wide flat plates under the chest and belly, each a thin slab with a dark outline strip). (2) Shoulder hump: a big rounded mass over the front shoulders (z 0.8..2.2, top y 3.5) that swallows all five neck roots (neckBaseC/IL/IR/OL/OR); at each neck base put a fat iron-and-leather collar ring (sweep ring of iron with 6 rivets and a leather strap), radius about the neck base radius (C 0.5, IL/IR 0.42, OL/OR 0.38) + 0.06, so the neck sweeps from the heads' builders slot out of it. (3) Front legs FL and FR: thick sweeps through shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints (radius 0.5 at the shoulder, 0.3 at the wrist, an armoured forearm), big paws with 4 chunky toes each ending in dark horn claws (cones, horn colour with hornTip tips), and a rear dew claw. Each leg wears an iron-bound leather cuff and a few overlapping armour-like scale plates (scaleLight). (4) Dorsal ridge: a row of 12 bone-coloured angular plates/spikes (extruded blades leaning back, tall and thin at the shoulders, getting lower toward the hips) seated on the top line of the torso from z=2.0 to the mount dorsalRidgeEnd, with boneDark bases. (5) Battle damage and Norse details: three deep scars across the left flank and one on the right (scar-coloured long thin slabs with pale bone ridge edges), a broken axe head (iron blade + rust edge, leather-wrapped haft stub) buried in the right shoulder, two snapped spear shafts (leather and bone) with iron arrowheads in the left flank, a chain remnant (chain-coloured torus links, about 10) draped across the chest ending in a spiked iron shackle, and rows of small carved runes (thin dark stroke parts with frost glowing inlays, glow kit) on the chest plate and each shoulder. Chest centre carries a big cracked bone-coloured breastplate shape with an ember glowing crack (emberHot).
parts.attaches: Neck sockets receive the head parts' neck sweeps at mounts neckBaseC, neckBaseIL, neckBaseIR, neckBaseOL, neckBaseOR; the rear of the torso (z=-2.4, width 1.2) ends where the tail begins at tailBase, and the dorsal ridge ends at dorsalRidgeEnd; the hindquarters part builds the rear thighs starting at rearHipL and rearHipR, inside the torso side. Rides joints hips, chest and the front leg joints.

parts.builds: The back end. (1) Rear legs BL and BR: massive digitigrade legs along hip/knee/hock/foot joints, with a big muscular thigh (radius 0.6 at the hip, tapering), a thinner shin angled back, a hock spur (bone spike) and a long foot with 3 forward toes and a rear toe, each with horn-coloured claws. Scales in scaleMid with scaleLight plates on the thigh front, bellyDark at the inner thigh, an iron-bound leather strap around each shin with 4 rivets, mud-dark (scaleDark) streaks at the feet. The left thigh has a chain-wrapped broken spear stuck in it. (2) Tail: a long thick tail from the mount tailBase (radius 0.6) through tail1..tail5, tapering to about 0.15 at tailTip (the tail tip must rest on y=0). Skinned to tail1..5, scaleDark on top, belly strip underneath, with a bone ridge of 14 plates getting smaller, and 5 spaced iron rings with spikes (a spiked war-collar look) along its length. The tip ends in a heavy bone-and-iron blade: a wide extruded leaf-shaped blade (bone with iron edges and a rust chip) plus two side barbs, and three runes glowing ember on the tail's flank. Some scars and one embedded rusted axe stuck in the tail's side, broken sword stubs, and a faded leather harness strap. A dark scar-coloured crescent wound on the rump with pale edges.
parts.attaches: Begins at mount tailBase, where the torso ends; rear legs start at rearHipL and rearHipR inside the torso's flanks (this part's thigh masses overlap the torso rear, z -2.5..-0.6), and the feet touch the floor at footContactBL and footContactBR; the tail ends at tailTip on the floor. Rides joints hips, tail1..tail5 and the rear leg joints.

parts.builds: The centre head C with its neck: the hero head, the biggest of the five. Neck: a thick sweep from neckBaseC through neckC1..neckC3 up to headC with radius 0.5 tapering to 0.36, scaleDark back with scaleMid sides, with a front row of bone-yellow ventral throat plates (about 8 slabs), a ridge of bone dorsal spikes (9, shrinking toward the head), a leather-and-iron collar with a few rivets mid-neck, and glowing ember runes (small straight strokes, glow kit) along each side. Head (skull from z 2.6 to 4.2, width 0.95, height 0.8, skull top about y 5.9): a heavy wedge skull, a long blocky snout with a flat top, a separate upper jaw and a separate lower jaw hinged at jawC (build the lower jaw as its own part on joint jawC, rest-opened about 8 degrees), both lined with thick off-white teeth (tooth colour; about 10 per side on top, 8 on the bottom, with 2 big fangs) set in mouth-red gums, a tongue (mouth) inside, and inside the mouth a faint ember glow. Face: two glowing eye (amber) spheres with eyeSlit vertical pupils under heavy scowling bone brow ridges (angular slabs), the left eye scarred with a long scar cut (scar with pale edge) across the brow and cheek; nostrils with small ember glows. Crown: four big back-swept curved horns (horn at the base, hornTip on the points, with iron cap bands and ember-glowing rune rings), two smaller cheek horns, and a fin-like frill of 5 extruded bone blades fanning back from the skull. A broken axe blade (iron with a rust edge) is stuck in the cheek, with a leather strap trailing. Chin: 3 bone spikes under the lower jaw. The mood is ember/molten: emberHot cracks on the snout.
parts.attaches: The neck starts inside the collar at mount neckBaseC (the torso part builds the socket); the head sits on mount skullC with the jaw hinge at jawHingeC. Rides neckC1, neckC2, neckC3, headC, jawC.

parts.builds: The two heads on the creature's left (+x) with their necks: inner-left IL and outer-left OL, each built with the same recipe as a smaller version of a hydra head (skull 1.35 long, 0.75 wide, 0.62 high; neck radius IL 0.42→0.3 and OL 0.38→0.27, sweeps from neckBaseIL/neckBaseOL through neckIL1..3/neckOL1..3 to headIL/headOL, bone [neckX1, neckX2, neckX3, headX]). Each has: separate upper jaw and lower jaw (jawIL/jawOL, rest-opened about 8 degrees) with rows of teeth and a mouth-red interior and tongue; two glowing eyes with slit pupils under angular brow ridges; nostrils; back-swept horns; a cheek frill of extruded blades; ventral throat plates and a dorsal spike row on the neck; a leather-and-iron collar with rivets. IL (frost head): frost-blue glowing eyes, glowing frost runes (glow kit) down both sides of the neck, horns of hornTip bone with frost-glowing crystal-shard tips, icy rime plates (scaleLight, frost) on the snout, a bone-coloured horn crown. OL (venom head, hangs lower and wider, angled down): venom-green glowing eyes, mouth and nostril glow in venom, drooling venom drips (small green teardrop parts) from the lower jaw teeth, a snapped-off left horn capped with an iron band, a long scar down the snout, a pair of tusks, and a chain with spiked iron shackle clamped round the neck. OL also gets rows of rust-coloured iron bolts along the jaw.
parts.attaches: Necks emerge from the iron collars at neckBaseIL and neckBaseOL (built by the torso part); heads sit at skullIL and skullOL, jaws hinge at jawHingeIL and jawHingeOL. Rides neckIL1-3, headIL, jawIL, neckOL1-3, headOL, jawOL.

parts.builds: The two heads on the creature's right (-x) with their necks: inner-right IR and outer-right OR, mirrored in position from the left heads but with their own identity. Each is built with the same recipe as a smaller hydra head (skull 1.35 long, 0.75 wide, 0.62 high; neck radius IR 0.42→0.3 and OR 0.38→0.27, sweeps from neckBaseIR/neckBaseOR through neckIR1..3/neckOR1..3 to headIR/headOR, bone [neckX1, neckX2, neckX3, headX]). Each has: separate upper jaw and lower jaw (jawIR/jawOR, rest-opened about 8 degrees) with teeth rows, mouth-red interior and tongue; two glowing eyes with slit pupils under angular brow ridges; nostrils; back-swept horns; a cheek frill of extruded blades; ventral throat plates and a dorsal spike row on the neck; a leather-and-iron collar with rivets. IR (venom head): venom-green eyes and runes (glow kit) down the neck, fanned horns in horn colour with hornTip points, venom-glow rim along the jaw, an arrowhead and a snapped spear shaft in the neck, scar slashes across the muzzle. OR (bone-and-iron head, hangs lower and wider, angled down): ember-glowing eyes, a heavy iron muzzle-cage (iron bands with rivets across the snout), a bone-plated skull crest of overlapping slabs (bone/boneDark), a broken-off horn on one side with a rust cap, long jagged tusks, chain links dangling from the muzzle band and a few ember glowing runes on the neck.
parts.attaches: Necks emerge from the iron collars at neckBaseIR and neckBaseOR (built by the torso part); heads sit at skullIR and skullOR, jaws hinge at jawHingeIR and jawHingeOR. Rides neckIR1-3, headIR, jawIR, neckOR1-3, headOR, jawOR.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a five-headed hydra in a gritty God of War aesthetic, with rune-carved scars, glowing marks, and frost/battle-worn texture. I'm planning the structure as a sturdy four-legged body with a tail and five long serpentine necks, dividing the build into body and neck/head sections for separate crafting.

Settling on five parts: bodyLegs, tail, headCenter, headsLeft, headsRight. Now I'm sketching the skeleton proportions — overall size roughly 7x6x9 units, with torso centered around the hips, four legs splayed, necks fanning out from the shoulders at varying heights and forward reach, and the tail extending backward to balance the total length.

Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy: a root hip joint, a chest joint, and then per-neck chains (base, mid, tip, head, jaw) following a consistent naming pattern so each head/neck builder can reference its own set of joints.

Now I'm sketching out actual coordinates for the body — chest position, torso box bounds, and leg placements for front/rear pairs — then designing each neck as an S-curve with three joint positions feeding into the sweep geometry.

I'm working out the outer limb positions, spreading the second branch's heads lower and outward for variety while keeping mouths closed in a resting pose, then checking the overall width budget comes out around 6.8 units. Now I'm setting up the head joint frames anchored at the back of each skull.

I'm figuring out jaw hinge placement relative to the skull geometry for the center head, estimating coordinates near the rear-bottom of the mouth, then starting to work through naming conventions for the limb joints since underscores aren't allowed in the regex pattern.

Settling on a naming scheme using prefixes like "IL" (inner left), "OL" (outer left), "IR", "OR", and "C" for center, applied consistently to neck, head, and jaw joints. I'm also laying out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, chest as child of hips, then neck segments chaining up to head and jaw, with legs branching off hips.

Now I'm figuring out actual coordinates for the hips and chest, then working through the rear leg chain for a digitigrade reptilian stance—placing hip, knee, hock, and foot joints so the leg bends forward at the knee and back at the hock like a bird or lizard leg.

Naming the four legs consistently (hip/knee/hock/foot for back, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand for front) using BL/BR/FL/FR suffixes, then laying out five tail joints trailing back and down so the tip rests on the floor.

Now I'm plotting the three neck-and-head chains (center, inner-left, outer-left) with arching joint coordinates and jaw positions, planning to mirror the inner/outer chains to the right side, before starting to list out the actual body parts beginning with the torso loft.

For the overall aesthetic I'm leaning toward a Norse God of War-style hydra: cracked stone-like scales, glowing orange rune carvings, embedded broken weapons from fallen warriors, fur pelts, iron rings, and scarred chest armor, with neck-root collars where the heads emerge from the shoulder mass.

I'm now picking out a muted, desaturated palette—swamp green-gray scales with darker shadow tones, bone-yellow belly, reddish scar marks, ember-orange glow for rune carvings, icy blue glow accents, and dark iron tones.

I'm also allocating my element budget: keeping the total under 900 units, splitting roughly 220 for the body/legs, 130 for the tail with spines and embedded axes, 150 for the central head, and 200 each for the left and right heads.

Each head part needs to own its neck geometry, sweeping from joints at the torso base, so I'm defining mount points like neckBaseC, neckBaseIL, and neckBaseIR with varying root radii—around 0.5 for the center neck and slightly smaller for the outer ones—anchored near the top of the torso.

The torso itself peaks around y3.3 at the shoulders, with a hump structure built by the leg system that buries the neck roots in its collar area; the tail similarly attaches at a hip joint mount near the rear taper of the torso, with its own base radius and a dorsal ridge running along its length.

I want to give the dorsal ridge a defined path using the torso's top profile line, tracing height values from the shoulders back to the tail tip so ridge plates can seat correctly at each station despite the torso and tail being built separately.

Continuing down the tail segments, I want the tip to taper and actually touch the floor, so I'm adjusting the radii and heights so the last segment grazes the ground, maybe adding bone spurs or a blade-like fin at the end for a hydra-style flourish.

I'm assigning the dorsal ridge ownership: torso owns the ridge on its back, while the tail owns its own ridge continuing down the length, so the boxes don't overlap. I'll flesh out the tail part further with bone ridge plates, a fan-shaped blade tip, and iron shackle rings with broken chain remnants for extra detail.

Then I'm rethinking the split so bodyLegs doesn't get overloaded—maybe the tail part should also claim the rear legs and haunches, leaving bodyLegs with just the torso, front legs, neck sockets, and chest, so the hindquarters become their own grouped region with its own bounding box.

Now I'm working through the polygon budget allocation across body parts: tail and rear legs with claws for hindquarters, then torso front with belly plates, chest armor, embedded weapons, and runes, plus three separate heads each needing their own budget. Adding it up I'm over 900 total, so I need to trim allocations down—reducing bodyFront to 210, hindquarters to 140, and center head to 150 to bring things back in line.

I'm settling on a grim Norse God of War aesthetic with scarring, embers and frost, rune carvings, and broken weaponry, then building out a restrained color palette of under 24 hues covering dark and light scale tones, belly colors, scars, bone, horn, iron, rust, leather, chain, and ember accents.

Now I'm working out the shared head anatomy — wedge skulls, snouts, brow ridges, horns, frills, glowing nostrils, slit eyes, jaws with teeth, necks with belly plates and spikes — and giving each head its own identity: the crowned center head with four horns and a scarred blind eye, the inner-left head with a horn crest, the outer-left head with a tusk and iron-capped stump, and the inner-right head with frost-blue runes, assigning each an elemental theme like fire, frost, and venom.

I'm settling on a final elemental assignment across the four heads — center as ember/fire, one head frost, another venom green, and considering a bone-spiked variant with an iron muzzle shackle and chain for added character — then moving into describing the rest pose with necks separated and mouths closed slightly.

Now I'm building out the joint hierarchy: hips as root, chest as parent, then the tail chain through five segments, assigning positions and directions for each to set up the spine and tail structure.

I'm also working out the rear leg chain from hip through knee, hock, and foot, estimating positions and directions so the leg bends forward at the knee and back at the hock before planting the foot with toes pointing forward.

For the front legs, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw joints down the chest, with the elbow angled back and the wrist curving forward into the paw. Then I'm setting up the neck joints branching from the chest, grouping each head's chain under its own named group like "headC".

Now I'm working out the skull mounts — defining the neck base, head center, jaw hinge, and mouth tip positions, plus torso and tail reference lines and foot contact points. I'm sizing the skulls: the center head longer and wider than the two outer heads, with the lower jaw proportioned similarly but slightly shorter. I'm also tapering the neck radii from base to head for each of the three necks before working out the sweep path connecting neck to skull.

Settling on final size [6.8,6.5,11.4] with the hydra centered on x, and linking the body's dorsal ridge seam to where the tail ridge begins. Now I'm thinking through part descriptions and lighting—using glow selectively for embers, frost, eyes, and runes since painted surfaces can't glow—and locking in the God of War style guide: brutal, chunky, scarred, cold desaturated palette with ember/frost accents, carved rune glyphs, bone, horn, and iron detailing.

Working out the neck and head joint chain coordinates and tangent directions, positioning headC and jawC so the skull geometry (spanning roughly z 2.5 to 4.6 with teeth included) lines up correctly with the third neck joint.

Continuing outer layer neck joints through to the jaw, then starting to lay out bounding boxes for the head and neck regions.

Defining mount points...

I'm figuring out how to type the function signature for buildHeadsLeft, deciding whether Ctx is already defined in scope or if I need a fallback type to avoid errors.

Now I'm planning the actual geometry: using catmull-rom sweeps through the neck joint chain from base to head, then constructing the skull and snout shapes positioned relative to the head joint's local coordinate frame, with a helper function to place points using forward/up/side offsets.

Working out the jaw hinge position relative to the head joint, then sizing the lower jaw to extend forward from that hinge roughly matching the upper skull's length.

The jaw's direction vector points slightly differently than the head's, so I'm thinking through whether to pose the jaw open after building it, since rigid parts attached to a joint should rotate along with it. I'll build the jaw geometry in a closed position relative to the head's orientation first, then apply the rest-open rotation afterward.

I should build all the jaw and teeth parts first, since their positions are computed relative to the head frame anyway, and apply the jaw pose rotation last so everything rides along with the joint. I'll make sure every part explicitly specifies its bone and anchor point rather than relying on surface attachment, keeping things consistent through local frame placement.

For head orientation, I realize geometries built with default world axes won't align with the slightly tilted head direction, so I need to apply the joint's quaternion to rotate local geometry axes into the bone's forward/up convention -- designing shapes in joint-local coordinates where X is right, Y is forward along the bone, and Z is up, then letting h.quat handle the actual world alignment.

I'm planning a helper function that places geometry at a joint using word-based offsets and the joint's quaternion, optionally composed with an extra local rotation for fine adjustments. I just need to confirm the quaternion is valid and current after posing, since I'm applying poses before placing geometry.

Since the head joint is the parent of the jaw, posing the jaw shouldn't affect the head's own transform. I'm aligning the jaw parts to the head's orientation first, then rotating the jaw open by roughly 8 degrees about world X relative to that base, which should look right even though the jaw's actual hinge axis differs slightly from head alignment. For left/right placement, I'm treating positive "left" as the model's +x direction in word-based offsets.

Now I'm sketching out the head's block dimensions — cranium width, length, and height in meters relative to the head joint, with separate scale factors for inner and outer layers, plus a sloped back-skull section to avoid a purely blocky look.

I need to work out the snout geometry too, but I'm catching an important subtlety: the local-direction helper interprets numbers as "model forward/up/left" rather than along the bone's own axis, which differs from how array-based frame coordinates work. I need to reconcile these two coordinate conventions before building the frustum boxes for the snout.

Setting local x to negative L confirms left offset, and I verify the quat orientation matches the aim direction convention. For the snout, I'm writing a tapered box helper that builds a unit BoxGeometry and remaps vertices along the length axis, interpolating width and height from base to tip.

Now I'm planning out the per-head part budget—roughly 100 parts each for 200 total—and sketching the cranium and snout pieces with layered colors (mid, dark top plate, light ridges) using tapered boxes at specific dimensions and offsets.

I'm working out the precise vertical coordinates for the skull: cranium spanning roughly -0.31 to 0.31, the jaw hinge around u=-0.2, upper snout from 0.2 down to the palate at -0.12, and the lower jaw sitting below with a small gap to form the mouth interior, figuring out heights and centers for each box so they align correctly.

I'm planning gum strips (thin red boxes under the upper snout and atop the lower jaw), a tapered tongue box using a darker mouth-red variant, and a small interior glow element near the back of the mouth to hint at venom, frost, or ember breath depending on variant.

For teeth, I'm figuring out counts per jaw (upper rows with fangs, lower rows) and realizing the part budget is tight, so I'll merge each jaw's teeth into a single geometry using BufferGeometryUtils' merge function rather than keeping them as separate parts. I need a helper that transforms each tooth's local geometry into model space using the head's position/rotation before merging, so the combined mesh sits correctly relative to the skull.

I realize ExtrudeGeometry is non-indexed, so mixing with indexed geometries breaks merging — I'll normalize everything to non-indexed with just position/normal/uv before combining. For neck details like the collar, runes, and spikes, I'll place them using sweep frame matrices along the neck chain, sticking geometry at each frame and merging to keep part counts low.

For rigging, I'll derive orientation from each frame's quaternion and assign each item a single nearest bone based on position along the sweep, bucketing merges by bone name plus color so the total part count stays under control, roughly 200 or so.

Now I'm working out the clock-angle convention for the neck — 0° marking the dorsal/back side and 180° the ventral/front side, but since the neck rises up and tilts forward at 45-60°, I need to reconsider which side actually counts as ventral once the tube is no longer purely vertical.

So confirming: 0 is up, 90 is −X, meaning left side is −90. Both runes sit at ±90, but I need to figure out which outward orientation applies to each head's left side specifically.

Now I'm working through the torso-to-neck connection: the collars form at the neck base, with each neck following a path through its segment mounts into the head joint. Since the skull spans forward to about -0.35 and the neck enters from behind-below, I need to extend the neck path slightly into the cranium so it doesn't poke through visibly at the joint.

I'll keep the existing joints for the curve and set color sectors so the belly and dark scale bands wrap around the body, with bone-yellow throat plates layered on top near the midline. Then I'll call the sweep function with the neck's joint list, radius, color, and sector settings to build the mesh.

Writing plate geometry code...

Rotating by −θ instead, with spikes shrinking in height toward the head, using bone and boneDark colors for the base cones. For the mid-neck collar, I realize a torus works perfectly since its axis aligns naturally with the tangent direction at that point on the sweep, so I can position it right at t≈0.45 using the frame's Z axis.

I'm computing the torus center by offsetting from the sweep point along the normal by the radius, then layering an iron band torus, a leather strap torus offset along the tangent, and six small rivet spheres arranged around the ring using cosine/sine positions in the frame's XY plane.

Now I'm planning the frost rune decorations running down both sides of the collar at roughly ±80-90 degree angles, sampling along the sweep path and building each rune from a thin dark carved base box.

I'm designing a rune glyph builder that generates stroke segments in a unit square, merging the glow-enabled inlay pieces per bone into buckets keyed by name, color, and glow strength so they render efficiently together. For orientation, I'm setting up each rune's local frame so it lies flush against the neck surface, drawn in the across/tangent plane with its thin thickness along the normal direction.

I'm working out the correct rotation math so each segment's box aligns with its intended direction vector, then adding a darker carved base patch beneath each rune's glowing inlay for visual depth, and composing the transform matrices for the sweep frames.

Checking that the rune patches sit correctly on the curved neck surface without excessive sag given the cylinder's radius, and confirming the geometry stays hidden properly on side faces. Now I'm starting to define the head builder function that will take a config object specifying tag and head joint data.

Still defining head config structure...

Checking the actual joint offset against my approximated hinge position, the discrepancy comes out tiny — maybe a centimeter or so of shift, which is negligible since rotating about the joint location barely affects the rest pose at this scale.

Now I'm verifying the skull geometry stays within the bounding box: checking that the snout tip, cheek frills, and swept-back horns don't exceed the box limits for width and height on both the outer and inner layers.

I'm also placing the eyes on the cranium sides, deciding on their position and outward-forward orientation, and working out the slit pupil shape as a thin dark box inset into each eye.

Still orienting eye geometry...

Working through the rotation sign so that the inner brow end tilts downward correctly for each side, I derive θ = −0.35·e, flipping sign depending on which side e represents.

Now I'm placing facial details: nostrils positioned near the snout tip with small flattened glow spheres and dark recesses, plus bone-colored bumps on the snout tip for texture.

I'm adding angular armor plates across the snout and cranium in a "God of War" style, then building cheek frills from five extruded blade shapes fanning backward per side, mapping each blade's local plane to curve outward and up from the head.

Working out blade orientation for each...

I'm fanning the frills horizontally like a triceratops crest, spreading blade directions from backward to outward angles with slight vertical staggering per spike, sized around 0.38-0.5 long and 0.14 wide, and coloring them bone with a darker band near the base.

For the horns, I'm planning backswept curved sweeps using catmull paths with banded coloring—bone-colored shaft transitioning to a frost-glowing crystal-shard tip, plus a small crown ring of bone spikes near the base.

I'm laying out the horn structure per head: two larger upswept horns plus two smaller secondary ones, computing their path points in head-local coordinates. For the "snapped-off" variant, I'm handling the left horn separately with an iron band cap replacing the crystal tip.

Still placing horn tip coordinates, checking they stay within the head-size constraint box, and making sure the backswept horn curve doesn't collide with the frill geometry near the cheek.

Now I'm working out teeth placement along the snout edge—seven teeth per side spaced along the tapering snout width, positioned at the palate's bottom edge, using small downward-pointing cones that need their rotation flipped to aim correctly in local coordinates.

I'm also adding bigger fang cones near the front, a small incisor row, more teeth lower down, and planning the curved tusks jutting from the lower jaw as called for.

Now I'm figuring out bone assignments: skull parts to the head bone, teeth and jaw plates to the jaw bone, and the tusks as sweeps that ride along the jaw's path. I'm also adding venom drip shapes—teardrop forms with a green glow—attached to the lower jaw teeth.

For posing, I'm applying the jaw rotation and head tilt last, after all geometry is attached, so the hierarchical bone poses propagate correctly. For the ice variant specifically, I'm placing frost-colored eyes, runic markings along the neck, crystalline tips on the horns, and rime plates along the snout, keeping the plates a darker frost tone rather than glowing.

I'm settling on a small custom palette for the ice variant—pale rime, dark frost, dark tongue, and dark mouth interior—plus a dark venom tone, and arranging a ring of bone spikes across the back of the cranium leaning backward for the horn crown. Now I'm starting on the other variant's specifics, giving it glowing venom-colored eyes and a glowing mouth.

For the venom-themed details, I'm adding glowing green venom pooling in the mouth and nostrils, hanging teardrop drips below the lower jaw teeth, a snapped horn with an iron band repair, a long scar with bone-ridge edges down the snout, paired tusks, a spiked iron shackle-and-chain around the neck, and rows of rusted iron bolts along the jawline. Writing chain link geometry...
